## Introduction
This is a brief demonstration of how DataSHIELD can be used to analyse a randomised controlled trial
across several sites. We use the Beat the Blues trial, which compared computerised cognitive
behavioural therapy with treatment as usual in people with depression. The outcome is the Beck
Depression Inventory (BDI), where a lower score means fewer symptoms. The three sites hold simulated
data generated from the original trial.

## Load packages
```{r packages}
library(dsBaseClient)
library(DSMolgenisArmadillo)
library(MolgenisArmadillo)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Log in to servers using DataSHIELD
``` {r login}
url <- "http://localhost:8080"
credentials <- armadillo.get_credentials(url)

builder <- newDSLoginBuilder()
for (server in c("groningen", "amsterdam", "barcelona")) {
  builder$append(
    server  = server,
    url     = url,
    token   = credentials@access_token,
    driver  = "ArmadilloDriver",
    profile = "donkey"
  )
}

conns <- datashield.login(logins = builder$build())
```

## Load data
```{r}
datashield.assign.table(
  conns,
  symbol = "trial",
  table  = list(
    groningen = "rct/data/site_1",
    amsterdam = "rct/data/site_2",
    barcelona = "rct/data/site_3"
  )
)

datashield.assign.table(
  conns,
  symbol = "trial_long",
  table  = list(
    groningen = "rct/data/site_1_long",
    amsterdam = "rct/data/site_2_long",
    barcelona = "rct/data/site_3_long"
  )
)
```

## Check what data is available
```{r tables}
ds.ls()
ds.head("trial")
ds.View("trial")
ds.class("trial")
ds.dim("trial")
ds.colnames("trial")$groningen
```

## Check the trial arms
We can check how participants were allocated to each arm at each site:
```{r arms}
knitr::kable(ds.table("trial$treatment")$output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts)
```

## Summarise data
View summary statistics for pre-trial depression score:
```{r summary}
by_site  <- ds.quantileMean("trial$bdi.pre", type = "split")
combined <- ds.quantileMean("trial$bdi.pre", type = "combine")
knitr::kable(rbind(do.call(rbind, by_site), combined = combined), digits = 1)
```

## Visualise data
We can look at a histogram of BDI before treatment, first for all sites combined:

```{r histogram-combined}
ds.histogram("trial$bdi.pre", type = "combine")
```

and then at each site:

```{r histogram-split}
ds.histogram("trial$bdi.pre", type = "split")
```

## Treatment effect across all sites
We estimate the effect of the therapy on BDI at 2 months, adjusting for BDI before treatment. We fit one model to the combined data, without moving it:
```{r pooled}
pooled <- ds.glm(
  formula = "bdi.2m ~ treatment + bdi.pre",
  data    = "trial",
  family  = "gaussian"
)
knitr::kable(pooled$coefficients["treatmentBtheB", , drop = FALSE], digits = 3)
```

## Treatment effect at each site
Alternatively, we can fit the model at each site and then combine the estimates, which is a meta-analysis:
```{r slma}
slma <- ds.glmSLMA(
  formula  = "bdi.2m ~ treatment + bdi.pre",
  family   = "gaussian",
  dataName = "trial"
)
est <- c(slma$betamatrix.valid["treatmentBtheB", ], slma$SLMA.pooled.ests.matrix["treatmentBtheB", "pooled.REML"])
se  <- c(slma$sematrix.valid["treatmentBtheB", ], slma$SLMA.pooled.ests.matrix["treatmentBtheB", "se.REML"])
z   <- est / se
effects <- data.frame(
  Estimate = est, `Std. Error` = se, `z-value` = z, `p-value` = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z)),
  `low0.95CI` = est - qnorm(0.975) * se, `high0.95CI` = est + qnorm(0.975) * se,
  row.names = c(names(conns), "Combined"), check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(effects, digits = 3)
```

Plot of the effect at each site and combined:
```{r forest}
sites <- names(conns)
site_est <- slma$betamatrix.valid["treatmentBtheB", ]
site_se  <- slma$sematrix.valid["treatmentBtheB", ]

two_stage <- metafor::rma(yi = site_est, sei = site_se, method = "REML", slab = sites)
metafor::forest(
  two_stage,
  header = c("Site", "Difference in BDI [95% CI]"),
  xlab   = "Difference in BDI at 2 months (therapy minus usual care)",
  mlab   = "Combined (two-stage)",
  ylim   = c(-3, length(sites) + 3),
  col = "#4285F4", border = "#4285F4", psize = 1.2
)
metafor::addpoly(
  x = pooled$coefficients["treatmentBtheB", "Estimate"],
  sei = pooled$coefficients["treatmentBtheB", "Std. Error"],
  row = -2, mlab = "Combined (one-stage)", col = "#E6B96A", border = "#B9852A"
)
```

## Does the effect differ between groups?
Because the model uses participant-level data, we can test whether the effect differs by antidepressant use:
```{r interaction}
interaction <- ds.glm(
  formula = "bdi.2m ~ treatment * drug + bdi.pre",
  data    = "trial",
  family  = "gaussian"
)
knitr::kable(interaction$coefficients, digits = 3)
```

## Change over time
BDI was measured at 2, 3, 5 and 8 months. A mixed model uses all of these follow-ups, with a random intercept and slope for each participant. For this the data are held in long format, one row per participant and follow-up:
```{r long}
ds.dim("trial_long")
ds.colnames("trial_long")$groningen
```

The model is fitted at each site and the estimates are combined. The `treatment:month` term shows whether the effect changes over time:
```{r mixed}
mixed <- ds.lmerSLMA(
  formula  = "bdi ~ treatment * month + bdi.pre + (1 + month | id)",
  dataName = "trial_long"
)
slma_table <- function(fit) {
  by_site <- sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", fit$betamatrix.valid, fit$sematrix.valid)
  by_site <- matrix(by_site, nrow(fit$betamatrix.valid), dimnames = list(rownames(fit$betamatrix.valid), names(conns)))
  combined <- sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", fit$SLMA.pooled.ests.matrix[, "pooled.REML"], fit$SLMA.pooled.ests.matrix[, "se.REML"])
  knitr::kable(cbind(by_site, Combined = combined), align = "r")
}
slma_table(mixed)
```

Trajectories need not be straight lines. We add a squared month term, created on the servers, and let it differ by treatment arm:
```{r nonlinear}
ds.make("trial_long$month^2", newobj = "month2")
ds.dataFrame(c("trial_long", "month2"), newobj = "trial_long")

mixed_nl <- ds.lmerSLMA(
  formula  = "bdi ~ treatment * (month + month2) + bdi.pre + (1 + month | id)",
  dataName = "trial_long"
)
slma_table(mixed_nl)
```

Plot of the combined trajectory in each arm, for a participant with the average BDI before treatment:
```{r trajectories}
est <- mixed_nl$SLMA.pooled.ests.matrix[, "pooled.REML"]
mean_pre <- ds.mean("trial_long$bdi.pre", type = "combine")$Global.Mean[1, "EstimatedMean"]

curves <- expand.grid(month = seq(2, 8, by = 0.1), treatment = c("TAU", "BtheB"))
therapy <- curves$treatment == "BtheB"
curves$bdi <- est["(Intercept)"] + est["month"] * curves$month + est["month2"] * curves$month^2 +
  est["bdi.pre"] * mean_pre +
  therapy * (est["treatmentBtheB"] + est["treatmentBtheB:month"] * curves$month +
               est["treatmentBtheB:month2"] * curves$month^2)
curves$treatment <- factor(curves$treatment, levels = c("TAU", "BtheB"))

ggplot(curves, aes(x = month, y = bdi, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(TAU = "#9AA0A6", BtheB = "#4285F4"),
    labels = c(TAU = "Treatment as usual", BtheB = "Beat the Blues")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2, 3, 5, 8)) +
  labs(x = "Months since randomisation", y = "BDI (lower is fewer symptoms)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```
